# MU — Catalysts

## TL;DR

The next scheduled catalyst is **Q3 FY26 earnings (~late June 2026)**. Micron has guided to $33.5B revenue (+40% QoQ) and ~81% non-GAAP gross margin. Between now and then, watch NVIDIA Vera Rubin ramp news, hyperscaler capex updates, and Samsung HBM4 qualification headlines.

> _This is bootstrap context dated 2026-05-01. The runtime swing routine must do its own fresh research and indicator analysis; do not anchor to anything stated here._

## Upcoming events

- **Q3 FY26 earnings — ~late June 2026** (Micron's fiscal Q3 ends late May). Guide: $33.5B ± $0.75B revenue, ~81% non-GAAP GM (Micron Q2 FY26 release, investors.micron.com).
- **NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform ramp** — first systems shipping CY26. Micron HBM4 36GB 12-high in volume.
- **Hyperscaler capex updates (May–July 2026)** — MSFT, META, GOOGL, AMZN earnings reset the ~$700B 2026 AI-capex narrative.
- **HBM4 customer qualifications** — Samsung pushing for NVIDIA HBM4 qualification (VideoCardz reports Samsung HBM4 entering mass production for Vera Rubin).

## Recent news synthesis

- **Q2 FY26 print (Mar 2026)**: Revenue $23.86B vs $8.05B YoY (+196%); Cloud Memory BU $7.7B, Core Data Center BU $5.7B, Mobile & Client BU $7.7B (Micron release, Futurum, tech-insider.org). FY26 capex raised to $25B+ from $20B.
- **HBM4 in volume production for NVIDIA Vera Rubin** (Micron press release, Tom's Hardware, StorageReview). Spec: >11 Gb/s pin speed, >2.8 TB/s bandwidth, +20% power efficiency vs HBM3E. Plan: 15K wafers/month HBM4, ~30% of total HBM capacity.
- **SOCAMM2 + PCIe Gen6 SSD** also in volume for NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems (Globenewswire).
- **CEO commentary**: Sanjay Mehrotra characterizes AI memory as a "multi-year structural shortage" (TheStreet).

_Pending — re-check on next refresh; Form 4 filings post-Q2 print are the relevant window. Raw filings will be reported here without interpretation when pulled._

## Analyst consensus

Published price targets (as of late Apr 2026):

- **DA Davidson**: PT **$1,000** (24/7 Wall St).
- **TD Cowen**: PT **$660** (raised from $550, TheStreet).
- **JPMorgan**: PT **$550** (raised from $350, TheStreet).
- **Morgan Stanley**: PT **$450** (models up to $52 EPS CY26, TheStreet).
- **Bank of America**: PT **$300** (upgraded from Neutral; PT lags spot).

Spot price $542.21 sits above all PTs except DA Davidson and TD Cowen.

## Last updated

2026-05-01 (bootstrap_2026-05-01). Sources: Micron IR, Tom's Hardware, Futurum, TheStreet, 24/7 Wall St, VideoCardz, Globenewswire.
